items.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: Well in that band they had Willie Smith playing lead alto and Juan Tizol, the great valve trombonist who used to be with Duke. And I stayed at Juan Tizol’s house.

ctx.x: Did you give him like a week’s notice this time when you left?

Yeah, I gave him proper notice this time, yeah. I played it straight this time. And after that, Benny was kind of semi-retired then. He was going to go back to New York and not do too much, so that left an opening for me to join Tommy Dorsey in 1947. And that was a great experience, a wonderful band. He had people in there like Charlie Shavers the great trumpet player, Ziggy Elman was still in the band then, Paul Smith on piano, and Tommy himself was just superb you know. I stayed with him for three years, and…

of us said “we have a chance to join Duke Ellington’s band.” So he looked at us and hesitated for about fifteen seconds, then he said “take me with you.” I’ll never forget those words you know. But he was a great man. Harry was a great player and a sensational band besides you know. But I did get a chance to work with him for a while. And then of course after that, of course with Ellington, there are so many stories about that band, and Ellington himself was an element of surprise, always. Because you never knew…

items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: After that, I roomed with Tizol a couple of times... When Tizol came to me after I’d been in the band a couple of months... Juan Tizol said, 'I told Duke that you write arrangements.'

ctx.x: Yeah. His saxophone’s at the Smithsonian.

Jimmy Crawford was another drummer with Jimmie Lunceford. They played the two-beat style, Snooky Young playing trumpet. After being with Harry, Juan Tizol told me, “I just talked to Duke. He knows about Willie Smith. I told him about you. He’s looking for a drummer.” So the three of us decided, let’s talk to Harry, since he’s only playing one day a week, and tell him we’ve got a chance to join Duke. So all three of us said, “Harry” – called him Hawk. “Hey Hawk. We’ve got a chance to join Duke Ellington’s band:…
So Juan facilitated that one – Juan Tizol – going over to see Duke.

items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: While I was out there, I stayed at Juan Tizol’s house. That’s how I got with Duke’s band.

ctx.x: When did you – do you remember the circumstances for joining that band?
When I left Tommy’s band, I wanted to study with Buddy Baker. I mentioned him before: my composition teacher. While I was out there, I stayed at Juan Tizol’s house. That’s how I got with Duke’s band.

items.title: 61531_Juan Tizol oral history interview
items.q: Duke Ellington and his orchestra played the title number with solo by Juan Tizol... and featuring... Louie Bellson... A little while after Louie joined, right? [INTERVIEWEE] Uh huh.

ctx.x: Oh, he was great. He was learning doing arrangements from Strayhorn, you know? He used to ask questions of Strayhorn about arranging.
Louie Bellson is a fine man.
